v.title: Hibs Boss Reedijk Calls Out Easter Road Jinx Rumour
v.excerpt: Reedijk denies Easter Road is cursed, insisting Hibs’ woes are tactical, not supernatural.
v.body:
## Quick take
Reedijk is calling out the myth that Easter Road is cursed after a seven‑month home‑win drought in the Premiership. He insists the club’s fortunes are in the hands of the players, not superstition.

## What happened
After a 1‑0 defeat to Rangers, Hibs’ manager Marink Reedijk dismissed the idea that the ground itself is the problem. He highlighted that the team has been performing better on the road, pointing to recent victories in the away fixture list.

Reedijk also warned fans against letting the “Easter Road jinx” dictate expectations. He stressed that a club’s identity is built on resilience, and that the current slump is a tactical issue, not a curse.

## Why it matters
- **Psychology of the squad**: Acknowledging the jinx could demoralise the players, especially after a long winless spell. Reedijk’s denial aims to keep the squad’s confidence intact, which is vital as Barcelona’s own title chase has seen confidence wobble after a recent defeat.
- **Fan engagement**: Hibs’ supporters are a passionate fan base. By rejecting superstition, Reedijk keeps the narrative focused on performance, mirroring how Barça fans rally behind the team during tough stretches, keeping the atmosphere electric rather than bleak.
- **Strategic implications**: The jinx narrative could distract from tactical adjustments. By cutting through the myth, Reedijk allows the coaching staff to concentrate on set‑piece improvements and midfield control—areas Barcelona has also been refining under new manager.

## What's next
Watch Hibs’ next home game against Celtic. Reedijk’s decision to abandon the Easter Road jinx will be tested as the pressure mounts. A win would vindicate his stance and could spark a turnaround, much like how a single victory can shift momentum for Barça in La Liga. Keep an eye on the tactical tweaks Reedijk may deploy—especially in the midfield—because that could be the key to breaking the home‑win drought.

*Source: [Hibs boss Reedijk rejects talk of Easter Road jinx](https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cr78274gepz0o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)*
